description: Jordaan gable houses that BAG dates after 1870 (rebuilds, restorations and infill behind a restored gable): the same 4-6.6 m red-brown brick front, ground storey and two or three upper storeys, drawn with the neck-gable body; the strip skyline must read a bell or point gable (rise 2.0-5.5 m, top 0.2-0.9 m) or the type is vetoed. Pick by cluster, not by one face: 32 held pands of 21 faces in the first batch

match.note: Held-pand cluster, Bloemgrachtbuurt batch 2026-10-29 (scripts/block-face/faces/*/auto-place.json, skyline read under clean sky): narrow gable pands built 1871-1910 (16 pands, 11 faces: eaves median 10.9 m, width 4.7 m, crown rise 3.2 m, top 0.5 m) and after 1910 (16 pands, 10 faces: eaves 11.3 m, width 5.2 m, rise 2.8 m, top 0.4 m). They share the neck-gable's body (3.6-6.6 m, 3-4 storeys); only the BAG year kept them out. Bell/point crown only: a neck gable (top 0.9-3.0 m) is not in the cluster. Likeness of the shared body is NOT verified here; the Opus strip review judges it. match.eavesM [7.5, 9.3] only sets the storey pitch (mid / 3 storeys = 2.8 m) so that 3 storeys at 7.6-9.2 m and 4 at 10-11.5 m (pitch 2.6-2.9 m) both score as this type; the cluster eaves run 7.6-13.1 m

neck.note: Bloemgracht 80-128 (168157): a neck gable 8.8-12.3 m with one attic light and the hoist beam over it

bell.note: Bloemgracht 16-32 (173345): a bell gable 8.6-11.3 m, one attic light

door-left.note: house door on the left axis; a pand whose door reads on the right is mirrored (mirrorForDoor), so a two-axis front keeps a valid door bay

rhythm.groundFloor: a house door and windows, or a small shop
rhythm.roofline: neck or bell gable with one attic light and a hoist beam
schemaLimits: the sandstone scrolls (klauwstukken) beside the neck are not drawn
the gable cap ornaments are not drawn
